new_packages.label: הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ וְשִׂמְחַת כָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת
new_packages.label_en: The Root and the Joy of All Goods
new_packages.reason: Five nodes share the essential nature of the unified, root-level joy. The Root (שרש) IS the state where all goods converge into one; looking upward at all the good (הסתכלות למעלה) IS the Root (text: 'דהיינו על השרש'); joy from all goods together IS perfect joy — they are two names for the same attainment; and Jethro (יתרו) IS the one who looks upward. All are parallel expressions of the single spiritual vantage point from which all goods appear as one.

bechina_edges_to_add.proof: וְזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר כִּי־אִם כְּשֶׁמִּסְתַּכֵּל לְמַעְלָה עַל כָּל הַטּוֹבָה, דְּהַיְנוּ עַל הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ
שְׁלֵמוּת וְגַדְלוּת הַשִּׂמְחָה הִוא, מִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִשְׂמֹחַ מִכָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת בְּיַחַד
וְשָׁם בְּהַשֹּׁרֶשׁ הַכֹּל אֶחָד, וַאֲזַי שִׂמְחָתוֹ מִכָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת בְּיַחַד
וְזֶהוּ: וַיִּחַדְּ יִתְרוֹ עַל כָּל הַטּוֹבָה... כִּי הָיָה מִסְתַּכֵּל לְמַעְלָה עַל כָּל הַטּוֹבָה, הַיְנוּ עַל הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ

new_packages.mirror_notes: Package NEW_A (unified root-level joy) is mirrored by Package NEW_C (fragmented divisions). Jethro who rejoices from all goods together is the polar opposite of the anonymous person who cannot rejoice from any good and instead experiences jealousy and anguish. The Root that unifies is the polar opposite of the Divisions (חלוקים) that separate.

new_packages.label: הַכְּלָלִיּוּת וְהַהִתְנוֹצְצוּת
new_packages.reason: Five nodes share the essential nature of the mechanism of luminous inclusion. Inclusiveness (כלליות) IS joy included within its fellow (שמחה בחברתה) — the text defines them in the same breath. Sparkling (התנוצצות) IS the light of joy (אור השמחה) — both name the same amplified radiance that emerges when joys are unified. The multiplicity of joys included together (ריבוי שמחות שנכללין ביחד) is the structural-quantitative face of the same reality. All five nodes describe what happens at the junction point between the Root (Package A) and the experience of joy — how the unified root generates amplified light through mutual resonance.

bechina_edges_to_add.proof: כִּי נִגְדָּל וְנִתּוֹסֵף הָאוֹר מְאֹד, עַל־יְדֵי הִתְנוֹצְצוּת שֶׁמִּתְנוֹצֵץ מִשִּׂמְחָה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ
כָּל מַה שֶּׁנִּכְלָלִין יוֹתֵר רִבּוּי הַשְּׂמָחוֹת זֶה בָּזֶה, נִגְדָּל וְנִתּוֹסֵף אוֹר הַשִּׂמְחָה
וְכָל מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ יוֹתֵר שְׂמָחוֹת שֶׁנִּכְלָלִין בְּיַחַד, נִתּוֹסֵף בְּיוֹתֵר וְיוֹתֵר אוֹר הַהִתְנוֹצְצוּת

new_packages.mirror_notes: Package NEW_B has no direct evil mirror in this Torah. The fragmented state (Package NEW_C) is the opposite of NEW_A (the root) rather than of NEW_B. The inclusion/sparkling mechanism has no counterpart force described — the Torah does not describe 'anti-sparkling.' The closest structural equivalent would be the isolated, side-by-side joys that never interact ('כָּל אֶחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ') — but this is subsumed in Package NEW_C under the domain of פירוד השמחות.

new_packages.label: פֵּירוּד הַשְּׂמָחוֹת — חִלּוּקִים
new_packages.reason: Three nodes share the essential nature of spiritual fragmentation — the condition of ordinary people (סתם בני אדם) whose experience of good is divided and separate rather than unified. Divisions (חלוקים) IS fragmentation (פירוד השמחות) — both describe the same structural reality of joys that cannot coexist simultaneously. Jealousy and anguish (קנאה וצער) is the experiential extreme of the same fragmented condition: when a person's fragmentation is total, they not only cannot rejoice from goods but actively resent others' goods. All three are parallel expressions of the same evil essential nature: disconnection from the Root.

bechina_edges_to_add.proof: כִּי יֵשׁ חִלּוּקִים רַבִּים בְּעִנְיַן הַשִּׂמְחָה... רַק מִכָּל אֶחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ בָּזֶה אַחַר זֶה
גַּם יֵשׁ אֶחָד, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם שִׂמְחָה כְּלָל... וְאַדְּרַבָּא, יֵשׁ לוֹ קִנְאָה וָצַעַר

new_packages.mirror_notes: Package NEW_C is the evil mirror of Package NEW_A. The Root-gazer (יתרו) who achieves joy from all goods together is mirrored by the divided person who achieves no joy from any good and instead falls into jealousy. The unifying Root (שרש) is mirrored by the dividing Divisions (חלוקים). The Torah's structure is a simple dyad: the holy person looks upward and sees unity; the ordinary fragmented person looks at the surface and sees only divisions.

observations:
LM2 Torah 34 is the shortest Torah in this dataset that has been analyzed. It is a brief, structurally simple teaching consisting of three conceptual packages:

1. NEW_A (Root and unified joy): 5 nodes, ~4 bechina edges. This is the Torah's central positive teaching. שרש is the dominant hub with 3 direct bechina connections. The key exegetical move is reading 'וַיִּחַדְּ יִתְרוֹ' as evidence that Jethro had attained the root-level perspective.

2. NEW_B (Inclusion and sparkling): 5 nodes, ~4 bechina edges. This is the Torah's mechanism package — describing HOW unified joy generates amplified light. כלליות is the dominant node. This package elaborates on what the root-level experience looks and feels like: joys spark off each other in mutual illumination, with the light growing in proportion to the number of joys unified.

3. NEW_C (Fragmented joy): 3 nodes, ~2 bechina edges. This is the evil/deficient mirror of Package NEW_A. חלוקים is the dominant node. The Rebbe uses the wedding scene to illustrate fragmentation — different guests rejoicing from different things — and then extends to the extreme case of someone who has no joy at all and falls into jealousy.

The Torah's argument in two moves:
[NEW_C: fragmented state] ←contrast→ [NEW_A: root-level unity] →eitza→ [NEW_B: luminous inclusion]

The good/evil mirror is simple and direct: NEW_A (Root/unity) mirrors NEW_C (Divisions/fragmentation). There is no evil wisdom figure, no anti-Torah, no complex demonic hierarchy. This reflects the brevity of the teaching — it is a single positive insight (look to the root) with its natural negative contrast (the divided state).

Note on existing eitza edges: The three existing 'cause' edges in torahData.js accurately capture the Torah's eitza flow and should be retained as typed. They represent: (1) looking at the root causes perfect joy; (2) inclusion of joys causes increased light; (3) sparkling from joy to joy causes the great increase of light. These are distinct from the bechina relationships proposed in NEW_A and NEW_B.

Cross-Torah connections: Several proposed nodes are likely to appear in other Torahs: שמחה (joy) as a domain concept, שרש (root/source) as a spiritual metaphor, כלליות (inclusion/totality) as a structural principle, and יתרו (Jethro) as an exemplar figure. The אור (light) and התנוצצות (sparkling) motif may connect to light-mysticism clusters in other Torahs.
